subject: Biochemistry
vignette: An enzymologist studies a purified kinase obtained from a patient with a rare congenital metabolic disorder. A Lineweaver-Burk plot of 1/v versus 1/[S] is constructed, with v expressed in micromol/min per mg of protein and [S] in mM. The best-fit line has a y-intercept of 0.02 and an x-intercept of -0.5.
question: Which of the following correctly reports the Km and Vmax of this enzyme?

options.text: Km = 0.5 mM; Vmax = 0.02 micromol/min per mg
Km = 0.5 mM; Vmax = 50 micromol/min per mg
Km = 2 mM; Vmax = 0.02 micromol/min per mg
Km = 2 mM; Vmax = 50 micromol/min per mg
Km = 20 mM; Vmax = 500 micromol/min per mg

explanation_correct: In the double-reciprocal plot the y-intercept equals 1/Vmax and the x-intercept equals -1/Km. A y-intercept of 0.02 gives Vmax = 1/0.02 = 50 micromol/min per mg, and an x-intercept of -0.5 mM raises to the minus first power gives Km = 1/0.5 = 2 mM. The slope of the line would be Km/Vmax = 0.04.

explanation_incorrect.A: This option mistakenly treats the intercept values themselves as Km and Vmax, ignoring that the plot reports reciprocals.
explanation_incorrect.B: A Km of 0.5 mM equals the magnitude of the x-intercept rather than its reciprocal, so this pairing of values is incorrect.
explanation_incorrect.C: This option correctly inverts the x-intercept to obtain Km but fails to invert the y-intercept to obtain Vmax.
explanation_incorrect.E: These values result from inverting in the wrong direction; neither 20 mM nor 500 micromol/min per mg follows from the intercepts provided.

educationalObjective: On a Lineweaver-Burk plot, Vmax = 1/(y-intercept) and Km = -1/(x-intercept), so both intercepts must be inverted to recover the kinetic constants.
